definition: to release new code so that users can use it
example: We plan to deploy the new version to production after lunch.
exampleEs: Planeamos desplegar la nueva versión a producción después de comer.
cloze: We plan to ____ the new version to production after lunch.
note: The noun is deployment. In meetings people also say 'push to prod'.

definition: to return software to an earlier, working version after a problem
example: If the error rate goes up, we'll roll back the release immediately.
exampleEs: Si sube la tasa de errores, revertiremos el release de inmediato.
cloze: If the error rate goes up, we'll ____ the release immediately.
collocations: roll back to the previous version
note: The noun is 'rollback'. You can say 'roll back the release' or 'roll the release back'.

definition: the slowest part of a system, which limits how fast everything else can go
example: The database is the main bottleneck in our checkout flow.
exampleEs: La base de datos es el principal cuello de botella en nuestro flujo de pago.
cloze: The database is the main ____ in our checkout flow.

definition: able to handle more users or data without breaking or needing a full redesign
example: We need a more scalable architecture before the launch.
exampleEs: Necesitamos una arquitectura más escalable antes del lanzamiento.
cloze: We need a more ____ architecture before the launch.
note: The noun is 'scalability'. Pronounce it SKAY-luh-bul.

definition: old and still in use, often hard to change
example: Most of the bugs come from the legacy code nobody wants to touch.
exampleEs: La mayoría de los errores vienen del código heredado que nadie quiere tocar.
cloze: Most of the bugs come from the ____ code nobody wants to touch.
note: 'Legacy' is not a compliment in tech. It usually means old and risky.

definition: to keep software working, fixed and up to date over time
example: Who is going to maintain this library once Ana leaves the team?
exampleEs: ¿Quién va a mantener esta biblioteca cuando Ana deje el equipo?
cloze: Who is going to ____ this library once Ana leaves the team?
note: The noun is 'maintenance'. Stress is on the second syllable: muhn-TAYN.

definition: to look for the cause of a problem and fix it step by step
example: I spent the morning trying to troubleshoot the failing build.
exampleEs: Me pasé la mañana intentando diagnosticar el build que fallaba.
cloze: I spent the morning trying to ____ the failing build.
note: It is one word, not 'trouble shoot'. The noun is 'troubleshooting'.

definition: to officially say that something should no longer be used because it will be removed
example: We're going to deprecate the old API at the end of the quarter.
exampleEs: Vamos a deprecar la API antigua a finales del trimestre.
cloze: We're going to ____ the old API at the end of the quarter.
note: Often used as an adjective: 'a deprecated function'. Do not confuse it with 'depreciate' (lose value).

definition: an unusual situation that can break code that works in normal conditions
example: Your fix works, but it doesn't handle the edge case where the list is empty.
exampleEs: Tu corrección funciona, pero no maneja el caso límite en el que la lista está vacía.
cloze: Your fix works, but it doesn't handle the ____ where the list is empty.
note: Also written 'edge-case' before a noun, or 'corner case'.

definition: a temporary way to avoid a problem without fixing its real cause
example: It's not a real fix, just a workaround until we update the library.
exampleEs: No es una solución real, solo un parche temporal hasta que actualicemos la biblioteca.
cloze: It's not a real fix, just a ____ until we update the library.
note: It is one word. As a verb you say 'work around a problem' (two words).

definition: the amount of work or data a system can process in a given time
example: After the change, the throughput went from 200 to 900 requests per second.
exampleEs: Después del cambio, el rendimiento pasó de 200 a 900 solicitudes por segundo.
cloze: After the change, the ____ went from 200 to 900 requests per second.
note: It is uncountable. Pronounce it THROO-put.

definition: a period when a service is not working
example: The outage lasted forty minutes and affected about a thousand users.
exampleEs: La caída duró cuarenta minutos y afectó a unos mil usuarios.
cloze: The ____ lasted forty minutes and affected about a thousand users.
note: People say 'we had an outage', not 'a fall of the service'.

definition: to make a bug happen again on purpose so you can study it
example: I can't reproduce the bug on my machine.
exampleEs: No puedo reproducir el error en mi máquina.
cloze: I can't ____ the bug on my machine.
note: Bug reports always include 'steps to reproduce'. The adjective is 'reproducible'.

definition: to release a feature or product to users
example: We want to ship the dark mode feature by Friday.
exampleEs: Queremos lanzar la función de modo oscuro para el viernes.
cloze: We want to ____ the dark mode feature by Friday.
note: Past form is 'shipped'. 'Ship it!' is a common way to approve a release.

definition: to rewrite code to make it cleaner without changing what it does
example: Can we refactor this function before adding more logic to it?
exampleEs: ¿Podemos refactorizar esta función antes de agregarle más lógica?
cloze: Can we ____ this function before adding more logic to it?
note: Stress the second syllable of the verb: ree-FAK-ter. The noun is 'refactoring'.

definition: something that stops you from continuing your work
example: My only blocker is that I still don't have access to the staging server.
exampleEs: Mi único bloqueo es que todavía no tengo acceso al servidor de staging.
cloze: My only ____ is that I still don't have access to the staging server.
note: In standups people ask 'Any blockers?'. Do not say 'blocking' as a noun here.

es: regresión (un error nuevo en algo que antes funcionaba)
definition: a bug where something that used to work stops working after a change
example: The last release introduced a regression in the login page.
exampleEs: El último release introdujo una regresión en la página de inicio de sesión.
cloze: The last release introduced a ____ in the login page.
note: In tech it always means going backwards, never a statistical regression unless the context is data.

definition: the list of tasks the team still has to do
example: The backlog is full of tickets nobody has looked at in months.
exampleEs: El backlog está lleno de tickets que nadie ha revisado en meses.
cloze: The ____ is full of tickets nobody has looked at in months.
note: Pronounce it BAK-log. 'Backlog grooming' or 'refinement' means cleaning it up.

definition: to combine changes from one branch of code into another
example: I'll merge your pull request as soon as the tests pass.
exampleEs: Haré merge de tu pull request en cuanto pasen las pruebas.
cloze: I'll ____ your pull request as soon as the tests pass.
note: Say 'merge into main', not 'merge in main'.

es: pull request, solicitud de integración de cambios
definition: a request to review your code changes and add them to the main project
example: Could you review my pull request when you have a minute? It's only about fifty lines.
exampleEs: ¿Podrías revisar mi pull request cuando tengas un minuto? Son solo unas cincuenta líneas.
cloze: Could you review my ____ when you have a minute? It's only about fifty lines.
note: People shorten it to 'PR'. You 'open' or 'raise' a PR and 'approve' or 'merge' it.

definition: the delay between a request and its response
example: Users in Asia are complaining about high latency.
exampleEs: Los usuarios en Asia se quejan de la alta latencia.
cloze: Users in Asia are complaining about high ____.
note: It is uncountable in most cases. The adjective is 'latent', which is a different word.

definition: an external library or package your project needs in order to work
example: We should update this dependency because it has a security vulnerability.
exampleEs: Deberíamos actualizar esta dependencia porque tiene una vulnerabilidad de seguridad.
cloze: We should update this ____ because it has a security vulnerability.
note: Plural is 'dependencies'. Pay attention to the spelling: -ency, not -ancy.

definition: a quick fix released right away to solve a serious problem in production
example: We pushed a hotfix last night to stop the payment errors.
exampleEs: Subimos una corrección urgente anoche para detener los errores de pago.
cloze: We pushed a ____ last night to stop the payment errors.
note: Usually written as one word. It skips the normal release schedule.

definition: a setting that lets you turn a feature on or off without deploying new code
example: Let's put it behind a feature flag so we can turn it off if something breaks.
exampleEs: Pongámoslo detrás de un feature flag para poder apagarlo si algo se rompe.
cloze: Let's put it behind a ____ so we can turn it off if something breaks.
note: People say 'behind a flag' or 'flagged'. Also called a 'feature toggle'.

definition: an early, simple version of a product used to test an idea
example: I built a quick prototype to show the team how the flow would work.
exampleEs: Armé un prototipo rápido para mostrarle al equipo cómo funcionaría el flujo.
cloze: I built a quick ____ to show the team how the flow would work.
note: Pronounce it PRO-tuh-type. The verb is 'prototype' too.

definition: the extra work you create later by choosing a quick solution now
example: We keep shipping features and ignoring the tech debt, and it's slowing us down.
exampleEs: Seguimos lanzando funciones e ignorando la deuda técnica, y nos está frenando.
cloze: We keep shipping features and ignoring the ____, and it's slowing us down.
note: It is uncountable. The full form is 'technical debt'.

definition: the time when a system is not available
example: We need to schedule the migration so there's zero downtime.
exampleEs: Necesitamos programar la migración para que no haya nada de tiempo de inactividad.
cloze: We need to schedule the migration so there's zero ____.
note: It is uncountable, so you do not say 'a downtime'. A short event is an 'outage'.

definition: to fix a problem or security hole by applying a small update
example: We need to patch the server before the vulnerability goes public.
exampleEs: Necesitamos parchear el servidor antes de que la vulnerabilidad se haga pública.
cloze: We need to ____ the server before the vulnerability goes public.
note: The noun is also 'patch': 'a security patch'.

definition: when new requests keep getting added to a project after it has started
example: The project is late because of scope creep; the client keeps adding requests.
exampleEs: El proyecto va tarde por el crecimiento del alcance; el cliente sigue agregando solicitudes.
cloze: The project is late because of ____; the client keeps adding requests.
note: It is uncountable. Pronounce 'creep' as KREEP.

definition: working only some of the time, without a clear reason
example: This test is flaky; it fails randomly about one time in ten.
exampleEs: Esta prueba es inestable; falla al azar una de cada diez veces.
cloze: This test is ____; it fails randomly about one time in ten.
note: In normal English 'flaky' also means unreliable about plans: 'He's flaky, he always cancels.'

definition: not fresh or no longer up to date
example: The cache returns stale data for a few seconds after an update.
exampleEs: La caché devuelve datos desactualizados durante unos segundos después de una actualización.
cloze: The cache returns ____ data for a few seconds after an update.
note: Also used for bread. In code, a 'stale' branch is one nobody has touched in a long time.

definition: using more words or output than necessary
example: The error messages are too verbose, so nobody reads them.
exampleEs: Los mensajes de error son demasiado verbosos, así que nadie los lee.
cloze: The error messages are too ____, so nobody reads them.
note: Many tools have a '--verbose' flag that prints extra detail. Stress: ver-BOHSS.

definition: strong and able to keep working even when things go wrong
example: We want a robust solution that doesn't break every time the input changes.
exampleEs: Queremos una solución robusta que no se rompa cada vez que cambia la entrada.
cloze: We want a ____ solution that doesn't break every time the input changes.
note: Spanish 'robusto' is similar, but in English it is almost always used for systems and code, not for people.

definition: not needed because something else already does the same thing
example: This check is redundant because we already validate the input earlier.
exampleEs: Esta comprobación es redundante porque ya validamos la entrada antes.
cloze: This check is ____ because we already validate the input earlier.
note: In infrastructure, 'redundant' can be good: a redundant server is a backup.

definition: still working with older versions of a product or system
example: The new endpoint has to be backward compatible with the mobile app.
exampleEs: El nuevo endpoint tiene que ser retrocompatible con la aplicación móvil.
cloze: The new endpoint has to be ____ with the mobile app.
note: Both 'backward' and 'backwards' are used. Add a hyphen before a noun: 'a backward-compatible API'.

definition: to make something run faster or use fewer resources
example: We need to optimize this query because it takes eight seconds to run.
exampleEs: Necesitamos optimizar esta consulta porque tarda ocho segundos en ejecutarse.
cloze: We need to ____ this query because it takes eight seconds to run.
note: US spelling is 'optimize'; the UK uses 'optimise'. Stress is on OP.

definition: to find and fix the cause of errors in code
example: It took me two hours to debug a single missing comma.
exampleEs: Me tomó dos horas depurar una sola coma faltante.
cloze: It took me two hours to ____ a single missing comma.
note: The pronunciation is dee-BUG. Do not add -ize or -ing in the base verb.

definition: to record information about what a program is doing
example: Make sure you log every failed request so we can trace the problem.
exampleEs: Asegúrate de registrar cada solicitud fallida para que podamos rastrear el problema.
cloze: Make sure you ____ every failed request so we can trace the problem.
note: As a noun, 'a log' is the record itself. 'Log in' (verb) is different from 'login' (noun).

definition: to watch a system's behavior over time to catch problems early
example: We monitor the API with alerts that go off when the error rate goes up.
exampleEs: Monitoreamos la API con alertas que se activan cuando sube la tasa de errores.
cloze: We ____ the API with alerts that go off when the error rate goes up.
note: Say 'monitor', not 'monitorize'. The noun 'monitoring' is the activity; 'a monitor' is a screen.

definition: the process of releasing something to users step by step
example: The rollout will be gradual: first 5% of users, then everyone.
exampleEs: El despliegue será gradual: primero el 5 % de los usuarios y luego todos.
cloze: The ____ will be gradual: first 5% of users, then everyone.
note: As a noun it is one word. The verb is two words: 'roll out'.

es: traspaso, entrega de trabajo entre equipos
definition: the moment when one person or team passes work to another
example: The handoff between the design and dev teams is always messy.
exampleEs: El traspaso entre los equipos de diseño y desarrollo siempre es desordenado.
cloze: The ____ between the design and dev teams is always messy.
note: The verb is two words: 'hand off the work'. Also spelled 'hand-off'.

definition: a short, fixed period, often two weeks, in which a team finishes a set of tasks
example: We committed to too many tickets for this sprint.
exampleEs: Nos comprometimos con demasiados tickets para este sprint.
cloze: We committed to too many tickets for this ____.
note: Use 'in this sprint' or 'for this sprint'. A 'sprint review' shows the results.

definition: to say roughly how long or how much work something will take
example: It's hard to estimate how long the migration will take.
exampleEs: Es difícil estimar cuánto va a tardar la migración.
cloze: It's hard to ____ how long the migration will take.
note: The verb ends with a clear /eyt/ sound; the noun ends with a softer /it/ sound.

definition: to decide what is most important and do it first
example: We have to prioritize the security fixes over the new features.
exampleEs: Tenemos que priorizar las correcciones de seguridad sobre las funciones nuevas.
cloze: We have to ____ the security fixes over the new features.
note: Say 'prioritize X over Y'. Do not say 'prioritarize'.

definition: to connect one tool or system with another so they work together
example: We want to integrate the chatbot with the company's Slack workspace.
exampleEs: Queremos integrar el chatbot con el espacio de trabajo de Slack de la empresa.
cloze: We want to ____ the chatbot with the company's Slack workspace.
note: Use 'integrate X with Y' or 'integrate X into Y'.

definition: to move data or systems from one place or technology to another
example: We're going to migrate the database to Postgres next month.
exampleEs: Vamos a migrar la base de datos a Postgres el próximo mes.
cloze: We're going to ____ the database to Postgres next month.
note: The noun is 'migration'. Stress the first syllable: MY-grate.

definition: a test that measures how fast or well something performs
example: Let's run a benchmark before and after the change to see if it's really faster.
exampleEs: Hagamos una prueba de rendimiento antes y después del cambio para ver si de verdad es más rápido.
cloze: Let's run a ____ before and after the change to see if it's really faster.
note: It can also be a verb: 'We benchmarked three databases'.

definition: to stop working suddenly and unexpectedly
example: The app crashes every time you upload a file bigger than 10 MB.
exampleEs: La aplicación se cierra de golpe cada vez que subes un archivo de más de 10 MB.
cloze: The app ____ every time you upload a file bigger than 10 MB.
note: A 'crash' is the event (noun). Not the same as 'freeze', where the app stays open but stops responding.

definition: to undo a change and go back to the previous state
example: I had to revert my commit because it broke the build.
exampleEs: Tuve que revertir mi commit porque rompió el build.
cloze: I had to ____ my commit because it broke the build.
note: Git has a command called 'git revert'. Do not confuse it with 'convert'.

definition: to set up servers or cloud resources so they are ready to use
example: Terraform can provision the whole environment in a few minutes.
exampleEs: Terraform puede aprovisionar todo el entorno en pocos minutos.
cloze: Terraform can ____ the whole environment in a few minutes.
note: Not related to the Spanish 'provisión' as supplies. The noun is 'provisioning'.

definition: a person or group who is affected by a project or has a say in it
example: We should keep the stakeholders updated on the delays.
exampleEs: Deberíamos mantener informadas a las partes interesadas sobre los retrasos.
cloze: We should keep the ____ updated on the delays.
note: Very common in corporate meetings, including at pharma companies.

definition: a short task whose goal is to learn something, not to build the final solution
example: Let's do a two-day spike to see if this library can handle our traffic.
exampleEs: Hagamos una investigación de dos días para ver si esta biblioteca puede con nuestro tráfico.
cloze: Let's do a two-day ____ to see if this library can handle our traffic.
note: 'Spike' also means a sudden jump: 'a spike in traffic'.

definition: the deepest reason a problem happened
example: We found the root cause: a missing index on the orders table.
exampleEs: Encontramos la causa raíz: un índice faltante en la tabla de pedidos.
cloze: We found the ____: a missing index on the orders table.
note: Say 'the root cause of the outage', using 'of'.

definition: a review of what went wrong after an incident, to learn from it
example: After the outage we wrote a postmortem and shared it with the whole company.
exampleEs: Después de la caída escribimos un análisis posterior al incidente y lo compartimos con toda la empresa.
cloze: After the outage we wrote a ____ and shared it with the whole company.
note: Literally 'after death', but in tech it is a normal word. Often 'blameless' to avoid pointing fingers.

definition: responsibility for a task, a system or a result from start to finish
example: Good teams take ownership of their code after it ships.
exampleEs: Los buenos equipos asumen la responsabilidad de su código después de lanzarlo.
cloze: Good teams take ____ of their code after it ships.
note: Say 'take ownership of X'. It is a positive word in workplaces.

definition: a backup option that is used when the main one fails
example: If the main API times out, we use a cached response as a fallback.
exampleEs: Si la API principal agota el tiempo de espera, usamos una respuesta en caché como respaldo.
cloze: If the main API times out, we use a cached response as a ____.
note: The verb is two words: 'fall back on' something.

definition: extra time, memory or work needed just to support something
example: The extra logging adds some overhead, but it's worth it.
exampleEs: El registro adicional agrega algo de sobrecarga, pero vale la pena.
cloze: The extra logging adds some ____, but it's worth it.
note: Uncountable here. It can also mean fixed business costs.

definition: a bug that happens when the result depends on which of two processes finishes first
example: The bug only happens sometimes, so I think it's a race condition.
exampleEs: El error solo ocurre a veces, así que creo que es una condición de carrera.
cloze: The bug only happens sometimes, so I think it's a ____.
note: Often hard to reproduce, which is exactly why they are painful.

definition: small, simple and using few resources
example: We chose a lightweight framework because the app is very small.
exampleEs: Elegimos un framework ligero porque la aplicación es muy pequeña.
cloze: We chose a ____ framework because the app is very small.
note: It is one word. The opposite is 'heavyweight'.

definition: to disagree with a request or plan and say why it is a bad idea
example: I'd push back on adding that feature this late in the sprint.
exampleEs: Yo pondría resistencia a agregar esa función tan tarde en el sprint.
cloze: I'd ____ on adding that feature this late in the sprint.
note: Use 'push back on' + the idea. It is polite and common in meetings. Also means 'delay' a date.
